h: Sincere Teshuvah Brings the Outcast Back Before Hashem

p: "This shall be the law of the metzora
on the day of his purification:
he shall be brought to the kohen" (Vayikra 14:2).
Even though before the sending away of the birds
he is forbidden to come into the camp,
וְיָצָא הַכֹּהֵן אֶל מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה וְגוֹ׳
"And the kohen shall go out of the camp, etc.,"
and afterward "and he shall bathe in water and be pure,
and afterward he may come into the camp."
and in another place simply 'the kohen'
and that is HaKadosh Baruch Hu.
'When the affliction of tzaraas is in a person,
he shall be brought to the kohen'
אִי הָכִי דָּא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא
if so, is this HaKadosh Baruch Hu?
for on Him depends all purity
That is, we do not find anywhere
that everything should depend on the kohen:
דְּכָל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא יָצָא מִפִּי הַכֹּהֵן טָמֵא
for as long as "impure" has not issued from the kohen's mouth,
and likewise the purification depends on the kohen,
as they said (beginning of chapter 3 of Nega'im):
וְכֵן בְּנִגְעֵי בָתִּים כְּתִיב (וַיִּקְרָא יד, לו)
And likewise regarding nega'im of houses it is written (Vayikra 14:36):
"And the kohen shall command, and they shall empty the house
before the kohen comes to see, etc.,
so that all that is in the house not become impure";
שֶׁכָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא אָמַר הַכֹּהֵן בְּפִיו טָמֵא
for as long as the kohen has not said "impure" with his mouth,
even though it is in truth an impure nega.
דְּהַכֹּהֵן סְתָם דָּא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא
that "the kohen," unspecified, is HaKadosh Baruch Hu;
is the agent of the Merciful One,
and a person's agent is like himself;
and Hashem Yisbarach sends into his mouth
And therefore throughout the parshah of nega'im
and that is HaKadosh Baruch Hu;
only at the head of the parshah is it written (Vayikra 13:2):
"And he shall be brought to Aharon the kohen
or to one of his sons the kohanim";
for a verse does not depart from its plain meaning,
that the kohen must see the nega
and declare it impure or pure.
נִרְאֶה שֶׁאֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק בִּכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
it appears that he has no share in Klal Yisrael,
and he is included in what they said
nor do they attain the paths of life'" (Mishlei 2:19), etc.
And about this it says "on the day of his purification":
וּמִן הַסְּתָם עָשָׂה תְּשׁוּבָה עַל הַפְּגָם
and presumably he did teshuvah for the flaw,
דְּאִם לֹא כֵן לֹא הָיָה נִתְרַפֵּא
for otherwise he would not have been healed;
"he shall be brought to the kohen"
who placed his head between his knees, etc.,
and a heavenly voice went forth:
is destined for the life of Olam HaBa";
and he acquired his world in a single hour.
אֲשֶׁר זֶה אֵינוֹ יָדוּעַ לְשׁוּם נִבְרָא
which is not known to any creature,
and as the Rambam, of blessed memory, wrote
until the Knower of secrets testifies
that he will not return again to his folly.
even a complete rasha, she is betrothed,
perhaps he contemplated teshuvah in his heart";
and it certainly speaks of a case
where he still conducts himself in his wickedness,
for if he had abandoned the way of sinners,
and if he still conducts himself in his wickedness,
שֶׁלֹּא לְפִי גֶּדֶר הָרַמְבַּ״ם זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
for, according to the Rambam's definition,
he has returned to his wickedness?
that at least at the moment
it must then be in truth,
to the point that the Knower of secrets testifies about him
that at that moment he abandoned the sin
so that had it presented itself to him then,
he would have abandoned the sin;
אַף שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ הִתְגַּבֵּר יִצְרוֹ עָלָיו
even though afterward his yetzer overpowered him
and he returned to his old ways;
but at the time of the act
וְעַל זֶה אֵין מֵבִין שׁוּם נִבְרָא
And this is "on the day of his purification,
he shall be brought to the kohen"
And in truth the meaning of "paths of life"
and not the life of this world.
And what they said in the Gemara there:
וְאִם יָשִׁיבוּ לֹא יַשִּׂיגוּ אוֹרְחוֹת חַיִּים
"And if they return, they do not attain the paths of life"
that is, it is impossible for him
to go by way of the paths of this world
and to come to eternal life;
אַךְ הוּא בָּא תֵּיכֶף לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם
rather he comes immediately to eternal life,
"There is one who acquires his world in a single hour";
and he need not go by way of the counsels
and the guarding of the paths in this world,
כִּי בְּפַעַם אַחַת בָּא לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם
for in one stroke he comes to eternal life,
as with Rabbi Elazar ben Durdaya.
And in Midrash Tanchuma it is expounded (Metzora 3):
"'He shall be brought to the kohen'
that is, he must by himself
אֵין הַדָּבָר תָּלוּי אֶלָּא בִּי וְכוּלֵּי
"The matter depends on nothing but me," etc.
And nega'im come because of seven things
and in the Midrash it is stated:
אֲבָל הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הִיא עַל גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ
which is the first enticement of the serpent,
"and you will be like God, etc.,"
that he take pleasure in himself,
"This shall be the law of the metzora
on the day of his purification"
"he shall be brought to the kohen"
as with Rabbi Elazar ben Durdaya,
to draw near to Hashem Yisbarach.
Although one need not do this kind of teshuvah,
עִם כָּל זֶה צָרִיךְ לִדְחוֹק אֶת עַצְמוֹ
and draw near to Hashem Yisbarach;
